implementerProof.how: I re-ran the implementer's token, revoke, replica and refused-history tests at 6176f738 under -race (5 of 5 each), and the two-build harness and browser spec against legion-envoy-v24.7.1 (13cb31a4). failures.criterion: A document that reads DOCUMENT_UNLOADABLE, which offers a rebuild, can be rebuilt (or the answer does not offer a rebuild for a cause the rebuild cannot repair). The architect named this finding.
failures.evidence: Real binary at 6176f738: a document whose doc_updates holds an update ygo refuses for its clocks (a delete range at 2^53, length 2) answers GET /text with 409 DOCUMENT_UNLOADABLE '... A rebuild from the latest saved version discards every edit made after that version. A person decides whether to rebuild the document'. POST /api/v1/artifacts/{id}/rebuild answers 503 DOC_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE, and again 2 minutes later. Red test (commit 49b70f3d): cd packages/envoy && go test -count=1 -run TestTheRebuildAStoredHistoryYgoRefusesIsOfferedRestoresTheDocument ./internal/dispatch/docs/ FAILs with 'the read offered a rebuild (the document's stored history cannot load ...), and the rebuild failed: document service unavailable: load document before rebuild: ...'. The test accepts either fix: a rebuild that restores the latest saved version, or a read that offers no rebuild for this cause.

failures.criterion: Architect item 3: a revoke while a large message is in flight delivers every message whole, then closes with 4412.
failures.evidence: ygo sends the 4412 close through gorilla's WriteControl, which waits at most 1 s for the frame write in progress. A page that does not drain within that second gets the connection dropped mid-frame; the server logs 'write to peer failed; closing ... use of closed network connection'. Real binaries at 6176f738: a writer page sent 30 x ~300 KB updates into the room while the revoked victim page (2,1) read nothing, then started reading. Reading at tick+0.3s and tick+0.7s gave 8 messages then CLOSE 4412. Reading at tick+2.0s gave 7 messages then CLOSE 1006 'unexpected EOF', 6 of 6 trials (4 in the large document, 2 in the small one). Round 5's code (3ac9da68), same scenario: 8 messages then CLOSE 1012, 3 of 3. Red test (commit c0b46985): go test -count=3 -run TestARevokedSlowPageReadsTheMessageInFlightAndThenTheRevokedClose ./internal/dispatch/docs/ FAILs 3 of 3 with 'ended with websocket: close 1006 (abnormal closure): unexpected EOF, want every message whole and then a close with 4412'. Its page reads 2 s after the revoke, within ygo's 10 s bound on a write. TestARevokeWaitsForTheMessageTheServerHasInFlight passes only because its page reads within milliseconds and one 1 MB message fits in the kernel's send buffer.
